memory_update.text: Local TV station owners are the cleanest public-market exposure for election-cycle ad spikes because political advertising revenue is separately disclosed by several broadcasters.
CTV platforms are increasingly important to campaign spend, but public-company exposure quality is weaker than local broadcasters unless political ad revenue is separately disclosed.

Potential follow-up candidates not included due to the five-name limit: The Trade Desk for programmatic CTV buying, LiveRamp for identity/data activation though acquisition status must be verified, E.W. Scripps and iHeartMedia for additional political media inventory, and public payment processors for donation flows where exposure is likely diluted.

Most campaign fundraising, voter-file, and compliance platforms such as ActBlue, WinRed, NGP VAN, Aristotle, TargetSmart, L2, and many FEC-compliance vendors appear private, nonprofit, party-aligned, or not cleanly accessible through US-listed equities.
Below-$1B exceptions may be justified in this node when political exposure is directly disclosed or unusually specialized, as with Gray Media, Sinclair, and Comscore.
NXST, GTN, and SBGI are the strongest direct US-listed candidates for the election ad stack because they disclose political advertising as a meaningful even-year local broadcast revenue driver.

ROKU is a plausible CTV political-ad inventory candidate, but political revenue contribution is not separately confirmed and should remain inference-level until management commentary or segment evidence is found.
RAMP is a plausible political data/identity-resolution candidate due to its DSPolitical/Catalist partner listing, but direct revenue exposure is unquantified and should remain hypothesis-level.

The Trade Desk, Amazon, Alphabet/YouTube, Meta, Disney, Comcast/NBCU, Paramount/Pluto, and payment processors may have second-order exposure, but this pass limited candidates to five; follow-up should test whether any disclose political/advocacy ad revenue or election-cycle commentary.

Most campaign fundraising, compliance, voter-file, polling, and FEC software vendors appear private or nonprofit rather than US-listed; public-market mapping may require second-order providers such as payment processors, CRM/cloud vendors, data brokers, and ad platforms.
NXST and GTN are the cleanest public direct exposures for local broadcast political ad cycles; verify 2026 pacing and battleground-market mix before ranking.
ROKU and TTD are second-order CTV/programmatic political-ad beneficiaries; exposure is plausible but likely not separately disclosed, so revenue materiality remains the key evidence gap.
SCOR is a below-$1B exception candidate because the March 2026 Comscore/Yahoo DSP Proximic Political Audiences launch is directly tied to CTV political advertising effectiveness.

Many high-relevance campaign fundraising, voter-file, and compliance platforms are private or nonprofit-linked: ActBlue, WinRed, NGP VAN/Bonterra, Aristotle, Catalist, AdImpact, Kinetiq, Mediaocean, and Stripe. Public mappings through PayPal, Block, Fiserv, Global Payments, or Blackbaud are likely too diluted unless filings or customer evidence show political vertical materiality.

LiveRamp/RAMP has relevant political data activation evidence, but a May 2026 definitive acquisition agreement with Publicis makes it a special-situation mapping rather than a clean ongoing US-listed candidate; keep in evidence but exclude from top-5 candidates unless the deal fails.
